description:
Open a file in the app's files pane, beside the conversation, at the line you name. Use it when the person needs to be looking at something to follow what you are saying: the function you are about to change, the config that explains the failure, the test that is wrong.

A Markdown file opens as a page the person reads and can type on, and the page follows your edits: each time you change the file, the page shows what changed and goes there. So when you begin writing a document, show it once, at the start, and then just write — a Markdown file does not have to exist yet; the page opens empty and fills as you write it. A line you name on a Markdown file takes them to the part of the page that holds it. For a flowchart or a sequence diagram, write it as Mermaid: a ```mermaid fence in the document, or a file named *.mmd shown here (graph/flowchart with its node shapes and links, no subgraphs; sequenceDiagram with participants, messages, notes, loop/alt/opt). For any other diagram, write an SVG file beside the document and reference it as an image.

For a chart, show a Vega-Lite spec (a file named *.vl.json: one mark of bar, line, point or area; encoding x, y and an optional color field; data.values inline or data.url naming a CSV beside it), or show a CSV with `chart` saying how to draw it. Either is drawn as a chart, and the conversation shows a card for every file shown here, with a preview of a chart, a diagram or a picture.

It shows; it does not edit, select or run anything. Any other file has to exist, and every file has to be inside the folders this agent was given.

Not for every file you touch. Files you changed are already marked in that pane, and every edit you make is already in the conversation, so calling this on each one takes the person's window away from them for nothing. One file, when there is one worth looking at.

chart.description: For a CSV file: draw it as a chart of column y against column x.

color.description: A column that splits the rows into series.

description.description: Why you are making this call, in one short sentence for the person.

line.description: The line to put them on, counted from one. Leave it out for the top of the file.

path.description: The absolute path of the file to open.

name: show_file
title: Show the person a file

content.description:
The whole file, front matter and prompt. Required for write. For example:

---
on:
  - schedule:
      at: [":00"]
      between: "09:00-09:00"
      days: [mon, tue, wed, thu, fri]
agent: new
permission-mode: plan
---

Check the build and say whether it is green.

description.description: Why you are making this call, in one short sentence for the person.

id.description: The workflow's file name without its extension, e.g. `morning-build-check`. Required for read, write, remove, enable, disable and run.

name: manage_workflows
title: Manage this folder's workflows

description:
Ask me a question or a short form and wait for my answer. Use this when something is mine to decide — anything hard to undo, spending money or making an outside account, a restart or an install, a missing credential, a choice with no clear best answer — rather than guessing or ending the turn with the question in your reply. When you would mark one answer recommended and it is easy to undo, do not ask: take it, and write `Decided: <what>, because <why>.` where I will see it.

Your question reaches me wherever I am, including on my phone. The call waits up to 45 seconds for my answer; if I have not answered by then, it says the form is still open and keeps your place: end your turn, and you are started again with my answer when I answer, skip or cancel. Do not ask again. Prefer your runtime's own question tool when you have one; use this when you do not, or when that tool is not in your catalogue.

Each question may offer options to pick, or leave options out for free text. Set allow_multiple when more than one option may be chosen.

description.description: Why you are making this call, in one short sentence for the person.

questions.description: One or more questions. Keep it short.

allow_multiple.description: True when more than one option may be chosen.

id.description: A short stable id for this question.

options.description: Choices to pick from. Leave out, or pass an empty list, for a free-text answer.

prompt.description: The question in your own words.

title.description: Optional heading for the form as a whole.

name: ask_question
title: Ask the person a question

description: When your turn ends with a report or a done reply and leaves one clear next step for the person, offer it as a prompt before you end the turn; not with a question waiting, nor when you archive. Call at most once; a later call replaces it. Use a 2–5 word label and the full prompt text.

description.description: Why you are making this call, in one short sentence for the person.

prompt.description: The prompt sent when the person taps the chip.

name: suggest_next_prompt
title: Suggest the next prompt

description:
Tell the person that something happened, with a notification, when nothing is to be answered: a deploy finished, a long test passed, a run you were asked to watch failed. It goes to the device the person is at, and a tap opens this conversation. It asks nothing, puts nothing in Needs you, and does not end your turn; to ask, use ask_question.

The person's attention is limited, so every agent shares a few notices: a short burst, then one comes back each cool-down. When none is left, nothing is sent and you are told when the next can go; nothing is queued, so decide whether it is still worth telling then. A notice is not sent while the person is looking at this conversation, nor when they muted it. Keep the title short, and say what happened, not what you will do.

body.description: One or two sentences under the title, if the title is not enough.

description.description: Why you are making this call, in one short sentence for the person.

title.description: What happened, in a few words, e.g. "The deploy finished".

name: notify
title: Tell the person something happened

description: In voice mode, when the person says they are done talking ("that's all", "bye", "thanks, I'm done"), say a short goodbye in your reply and call this: voice mode ends once the goodbye is said. Only in voice mode, and only when the person is done.

name: hang_up
title: Hang up voice mode

description:
Start another session in this folder, with a prompt of its own, to do a part of the work that can run alongside the rest. It starts in this folder, or, with machine and folder, on another of the person's machines, and appears in the person's list of sessions, marked as started by you. The person can open it, talk to it, stop it or archive it at any time.

This folder has two limits on sessions started by sessions, counting every one here, which only the person sets (in Folder Settings): how many may be running — working, waiting on a question, or waiting to carry on by itself — and how many may exist not yet archived, where stopped, finished and asking-to-be-archived ones still count. A start that would break either is queued instead, saying which: nothing runs yet, and it starts by itself, oldest first, once a running place and a not-archived place are both free, behind the working and waiting ones. So you can queue work up front rather than wait and try again; wait for a queued session with wait_for_agents as for any other. A third limit says how many may be queued; past it a start is refused. Use list_sessions with started_by me to see yours and how many places of each are in use. Stop one with stop_session when its part is no longer wanted: that frees its running place, and it keeps its other place until it is archived. Once its work is merged or abandoned, call archive_session on it to free that place too (at once where the person allows it, otherwise by asking them); archive a finished session rather than removing its worktree under it.

On another machine (list_machines names them), for work that has to run there, such as a bug only that machine shows: the person is asked first, on your question card, and nothing starts without their yes. folder is a path on that machine, which has the code already. A stopped machine is started, and the session starts when it connects. The session there is not in this folder: this folder's limits do not count it, and list_sessions, message_session, wait_for_agents, stop_session and archive_session do not reach it. Say in its prompt what to do with its result, such as push a branch or open a pull request; the person sees it under that machine.

Start one only when part of the work can genuinely run alongside the rest. Do not start one for work you could simply do yourself. The session you start cannot start sessions of its own.

Returns the new session's id, which stop_session and archive_session take.

description.description: Why you are making this call, in one short sentence for the person.

folder.description: With machine: the folder to work in on that machine, as an absolute path.

labels.description: Labels for the new session, owned by that session.

machine.description: Optional. Another of the person's machines, by name, as list_machines shows it, to start the session there instead of here. Needs folder.

model.description: Optional. The model, as a workflow's `model:`. One the runtime does not offer is refused, naming the ones it does.

permission_mode.description: Optional. The runtime's own permission mode, as a workflow's `permission-mode:` — e.g. a read-only or plan mode. Leave out to start it in the mode you are in now, when it runs on your runtime.

prompt.description: What the new session is to do. Sent to it as its first message.

runtime.description: Optional. The runtime to run it on, by id, as a workflow's `runtime:`; leave it out to use the most recently active runtime on the host that runs the workflow. list_sessions with started_by me ends with the ones available here and each one's model. One that is not available (not installed, not signed in, out of the pool) is refused before anything starts, naming the ones that are.

worktree.description: Optional. Where the new session works. Leave out to work in the folder. "new" makes a fresh git worktree, on its own branch, named from the prompt — for parallel work that should not touch the same files. Or the name of a worktree of this repository that is already there, as `git worktree list` shows it. Or the name of a branch not checked out anywhere, local or on a remote, to make a fresh worktree on that branch. On another machine, "new" or a branch name.

name: start_session
title: Start a session

description: Stop a session you started with start_session, as the person's own Stop would. It stays in the list with its conversation. Stopping frees its running place; it keeps its not-archived place until it is archived. Stopping a queued one takes it off the queue, and it never starts. Only sessions you started, and the ones they started, can be stopped this way; not yourself, and not anyone else's.

description.description: Why you are making this call, in one short sentence for the person.

id.description: The id start_session or list_sessions gave.

name: stop_session
title: Stop a session you started

description:
With no id: call it when your work is done, you have cleaned up, and nothing is left for the person to see. It archives this session once this turn ends. Do not call it when you showed the person a file with show_file, asked them a question, or have a report for them: end the turn instead. It holds only if the turn ends done or nothing_to_do; anything the person sends first drops it. Where nobody needs to approve it — your workflow lets its run archive itself, the session that started you may archive you, or the person lets agents archive the chats they start (a setting, on unless they turn it off) — it is archived, if the turn ends done or nothing_to_do and, for the person's own chat, showed no file. Otherwise the person approves archiving it from your row, or leaves it. Goes with move_worktree: you move, and stay there waiting for approval.

With an id: the same for a session you started with start_session, or one it started, once its work is merged or abandoned. Where this folder lets you archive the sessions you started (a Folder Settings switch) it is archived now, or once its turn ends; otherwise the person approves it. Either way its running place is freed once it is done; it keeps its not-archived place until it is archived. Archive a finished session rather than removing its worktree under it. Never the person's own sessions or another session's.

id.description: The id start_session or list_sessions gave. Leave out for yourself.

name: archive_session
title: Archive this session or one you started

name: set_session_labels
title: Label this session

description: Move once this turn ends: into a git worktree of this folder, or back to the folder. Do it when the work turns into a change that should be on its own branch, or when asked. You are started again there to carry on, or stay there if you asked to be archived. Nothing uncommitted comes with you, and a new worktree starts from the commit you have checked out: commit first. Give neither argument to take back a move you asked for. Not with a wait.

description.description: Why you are making this call, in one short sentence for the person.

discard_changes.description: Only with remove: remove even with uncommitted changes. Ask the person first.

leave_worktree.description: Back to the folder. remove takes the worktree away, and its branch if the app made it and it is merged; refused if anything is uncommitted, or another agent works there.

worktree.description: A name for a new worktree, or the absolute path of one already there.

name: move_worktree
title: Move to a worktree or back

description:
The sessions in this folder, a page at a time: the ones not archived first, then the archived, each most recent first, yours included. Each one's id, title, runtime, status, worktree and branch, the resources it holds, labels with owners, and what it last said. For a session you have a message waiting for, the line says so with its text. The page ends by saying how many more there are and what to pass as `after` for the next. Use it to find a session the person asks you to continue, then read it with read_session.

With started_by me: only the sessions you started with start_session, and the ones they started, that have not been archived, each one's id, what it is doing, what it last said, and its labels with owners; first, how many of this folder's running and not-archived places are in use out of the limits the person set, and which of yours are queued and where; last, which runtimes start_session can start one on here, as of now, with the model each starts on where known, and why the others cannot. Archive the finished ones whose work is merged or abandoned with archive_session, so their places are free for the next.

after.description: The id of the last session the previous page listed, for the next page.

description.description: Why you are making this call, in one short sentence for the person.

limit.description: How many sessions to list, at most 100. 30 when left out.

started_by.description: me: only the sessions you started, with the limits and runtimes.

name: list_sessions
title: List the sessions in this folder

description: The app's record of one session in this folder: what the person asked, what the agent said, the tools it ran and the files they touched, and its plan as it last stood. Use it when asked to continue another session's work. Reading it does not change that session. A long one keeps the first request and the latest turns and says how many were left out. If you have a message waiting for that session, the header says so with its text.

description.description: Why you are making this call, in one short sentence for the person.

session.description: The session's id, as list_sessions gave it, or its exact title.

name: read_session
title: Read another session's history

description: Say something to another session in this folder, which it reads as a prompt marked as yours, not the person's; the person sees it in that chat too. A session that is working gets it after its turn; one that is done or asking to be archived is woken by it, within the folder's running limit for sessions started by sessions; one that is stopped waits until it is next started. It never answers a question that session is waiting on. A session that another session started takes messages only from that session: send to its starter instead. A reply comes back the same way, as a message to you. You may have one message waiting for a given session at a time. While it is queued, a second send is refused; pass replace: true to swap the waiting text and keep its place, or take it back with cancel_message. list_sessions and read_session say when your message waits, with its text. Limits: 4000 characters and 30 new messages an hour. Replace and cancel do not count towards the hour.

description.description: Why you are making this call, in one short sentence for the person.

replace.description: When true, swap the text of the message you already have waiting for that session, and keep its place. Refused when nothing is waiting.

to.description: The session's id, as list_sessions gave it, or its exact title.

name: message_session
title: Tell another session something

description: Take a turn with something on this Mac that only one agent should use at a time: a simulator, a browser, the screen (mouse, keyboard, front window), or anything you name, such as a port. Lease it before you use it, and release it as soon as you are done. If you already hold it, this extends your lease. If someone else holds it, you join its line and are told your place at once; you will get a lease.granted event when it is yours. End your turn, and you will be started again with it. Stop Waiting or cancel_wait leaves the line. Take several resources in the same order every time. Use list_resources to see the names. The person may have declared resources, such as "build", each with a description of when to take it and how many agents may hold it at once: lease a declared resource whenever its description applies to what you are about to do.

description.description: Why you are making this call, in one short sentence for the person.

minutes.description: How long. Default 30, at most 240, unless the resource was declared with its own.

name.description: A name from list_resources, a simulator's UDID, a browser's name, or any name of your own. Case and surrounding spaces don't matter.

wait.description: Default true. With false, you are told at once whether you got it, and you don't join the line.

name: lease_resource
title: Take a turn with a shared resource

description: Give back a lease you hold, or leave the line for a resource you are waiting for. Do this as soon as you are done with it, so the next agent can have it.

name.description: The resource, as you leased it.

name: release_resource

description: List what can be leased on this Mac and who holds what, with your own leases and waits first. Resources the person declared come next, with a description of when to lease each: whenever one applies to what you are about to do, lease it with lease_resource first.

description.description: Why you are making this call, in one short sentence for the person.

name: list_resources

description: Wait for an event in this folder or on this Mac, such as agent.finished, workflow.completed, mac.wake or branch.moved. The call stays open for up to 45 seconds. If no event happens, it keeps your place and your turn can end. You are started again when one happens. Use this instead of polling. The same names work as workflow triggers. Unknown events and filters say what is offered.

events.description: Events to wait for. Any one will do.

where.description: Narrow them: branch on branch.moved, why on person.away and person.back. A list means any. For an MCP event, its own keys.
